questions.question:
A palindrome is a word that reads the same forwards and backwards. In a game of words, a player has the following two plates painted with letters.

From the additional plates given in the options, which one of the combinations of additional plates would allow the player to construct a five-letter palindrome. The player should use all the five plates exactly once. The plates can be rotated in their plane.
questions.explanation:
A 5-letter palindrome has the form X Y Z Y X, so letters must pair up around a middle letter. We already have A and D.

Option B gives R, an upside-down A and a mirrored R. Rotating the plates gives R, A, R, which makes R A D A R [latex]\text{---}[/latex] a palindrome using all 5 plates.

The other options cannot form matching pairs around a middle letter.

Answer: B

questions.question:
A series of natural numbers [latex]F_1,F_2,F_3,F_4,F_5,F_6,F_7,... [/latex] obeys [latex]F_{n+1}=F_n+F_{n-1} [/latex] for all integers [latex]n \geq 2[/latex].
If [latex]F_6=37[/latex], and [latex]F_7=60[/latex], then what is [latex]F_1[/latex]?
questions.explanation:
Work backwards using [latex]F_{n-1}=F_{n+1}-F_n[/latex]:
- [latex]F_5=60-37=23[/latex]
- [latex]F_4=37-23=14[/latex]
- [latex]F_3=23-14=9[/latex]
- [latex]F_2=14-9=5[/latex]
- [latex]F_1=9-5=4[/latex]

Answer: 4

then, the value of [latex] \frac{p^4+q^4}{p^2 q^2} [/latex] is

[latex]\dfrac{p^4+q^4}{p^2q^2}=79[/latex]

Answer: 79

questions.question:
Combinatorics deals with problems involving counting. For example, "How many distinct arrangements of [latex]\text{N}[/latex] distinct objects in [latex]\text{M}[/latex] spaces on a circle are possible?" is a typical problem in combinatorics. This kind of counting is sometimes used in the modeling of several physical phenomena. Often, in such models, the different combinatorial possibilities are assigned probability values. Assigning probabilities enables the computation of the average values of physical quantities.

Consider the following statements:
[latex]\text{P}:[/latex] Combinatorics is always invoked in the modeling of physical phenomena.
[latex]\text{Q}:[/latex] Modeling some physical phenomena involves assigning probabilities to combinatorial possibilities in order to compute average values of physical quantities.

Based on the passage above, what can be inferred about statements [latex]\textbf{P}[/latex] and [latex]\textbf{Q}?[/latex]

options.A: P is False and Q is False
options.B: P is False and Q is True
options.C: P is True and Q is False
options.D: P is True and Q is True

questions.explanation:
The passage explains that combinatorics is sometimes ("often," "in such models") used when modeling physical phenomena by assigning probabilities to combinatorial possibilities — it never claims combinatorics is always invoked in every physical model.

- P ("Combinatorics is always invoked...") over-generalizes what the passage actually says (which uses qualifiers like "often" and "sometimes," not "always"). So P is False.
- Q ("Modeling some physical phenomena involves assigning probabilities to combinatorial possibilities to compute average values") is a direct restatement of what the passage explicitly says. So Q is True.

Answer: P is False and Q is True

questions.question:
For positive real numbers [latex]S[/latex] and [latex]K[/latex], the function [latex]H_{K}(S)[/latex] is defined as: [latex]H_{K}(S)=\max (S-K, 0)[/latex]. The max function is defined as:

[latex] \max (a, b)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} a, & \text { when } a>b \\ b, & \text { when } a \leq b \end{array}\right. [/latex]

The graph below shows the plot of a function [latex]N(S)[/latex] versus [latex]S[/latex].
[latex]N(S)[/latex] can be expressed as ________.
questions.explanation:
[latex]H_K(S)=\max(S-K,0)[/latex] is the standard "ramp"/hinge function: it is [latex]0[/latex] for [latex]S\le K[/latex], and rises linearly with slope [latex]1[/latex] for [latex]S>K[/latex].

The plotted function [latex]N(S)[/latex] (from the figure) is [latex]0[/latex] up to [latex]S=10[/latex], then rises with slope [latex]1[/latex] from [latex]S=10[/latex] to [latex]S=20[/latex], and then becomes flat (constant) again for [latex]S>20[/latex] — a shape that increases and then saturates.

This exact shape is produced by taking one upward ramp starting at [latex]10[/latex] and cancelling its slope beyond [latex]20[/latex] using a second ramp of opposite sign starting at [latex]20[/latex]:
[latex]N(S)=H_{10}(S)-H_{20}(S)[/latex]

For [latex]S\le10[/latex]: both terms are [latex]0[/latex] → [latex]N=0[/latex]. For [latex]1020[/latex]: [latex]H_{10}(S)=S-10[/latex], [latex]H_{20}(S)=S-20[/latex] → [latex]N=(S-10)-(S-20)=10[/latex] (flat/saturated), matching the graph.

Answer: [latex]H_{10}(S)-H_{20}(S)[/latex]
